Water is hypotonic, so using it for bladder washout risks haemolysis (haemoglobinuria, possible acute kidney injury) and dilutional hyponatraemia if absorbed, which is why isotonic saline is standard. Of the two options in the team note, "Bladder washout may be unsuccessful" fits better than "Fluid may bypass," but neither names the haemolysis or hyponatraemia hazard, so I'd check the note's source before relying on it.
